messages:
maria: quick q — for the canary rollout page can we surface a per-model cost preview that shows token-level cost plus an amortized 'cache warmup' line? users keep asking why early canary runs look so expensive.

jake: yes, we discussed something like that in last week's design sync. core ask: show 1) per-token cost (model+sku) 2) cache savings ramp (prefix hit% over time) 3) projected steady-state cost. small mockup: https://redwood.internal/cost-preview

sarah: would help a lot. important: cache warmup attribution needs to be deterministic per-route so billing teams can reason about credits. otherwise it's a support nightmare.

maria: agree. sketch idea: show two curves — measured cost during canary and projected cost after cache warmed (with dashed line). also expose the assumptions (sample rate, avg seq len, prefix reuse rate).

tom: FYI we already emit per-invocation telemetry: model_sku, token_in, token_out, cache_hit_flag, route_id. but we don't currently expose prefix reuse rate aggregated by route in the console. we'd need a small telemetry aggregation job.

jake: can we estimate warmup amortization client-side using existing metrics? maybe compute weighted moving average of cache_hit_flag over sliding window and extrapolate steady state. low-lift and avoids new infra.

sarah: that could work as a first pass, but we need to be explicit about uncertainty. add a confidence band and a note: "based on sampled telemetry at 5%".

maria: UX ask: include a toggle in rollout UI: [ Show cost preview ] with options -> (a) Live measured (b) Steady-state projection (c) Both. default to both.

tom: implementation nit: the moving avg approach needs to account for model switches (e.g., fallback to smaller quantized models). cache hit semantics change across model variants. we should limit projection to the active model SKU or show per-SKU lines.

jake: +1. also we should surface per-token unit economics: tokens*model_unit_price + infra_surcharge. schema example we discussed earlier: 
```
{
  "route_id": "string",
  "model_sku": "string",
  "tokens_in": number,
  "tokens_out": number,
  "cache_hit": boolean
}
```
but for the console card we show a small derived row: [avg seq len, avg tokens per invocation, avg token cost, cache hit %, projected cost/hr].

maria: ops question — will this be behind a feature flag? we don't want to expose noisy projections to customers until it's stable.

ops-bot: feature-flag created: ff/cost-preview-rolling-2026. scope: internal beta. owner: @maria.

sarah: also add a path to opt-out of showing projection in invoices. team asks that billing numbers remain based on raw measured billed tokens. projection is only advisory.

tom: agreed. technical checklist: 1) aggregation job for route+sku hit-rate, 2) client-side projection service (JS) with fallback to server calc, 3) console card + toggle + confidence band, 4) docs + help copy.

jake: small perf note: computing moving avg on demand for very high-card routes might be heavy. prefer precomputed time-series (1m buckets) per route. storage cost is small if we sample.

maria: plan: I'll prototype UI with a stubbed endpoint (returns projected curves) and queue an infra spike to evaluate precompute cost. pairing with @tom next Thurs.

sarah: thanks. can you include an example copy for the confidence tooltip? suggestion: "Projected cost assumes cache reuse and steady request mix; actual billed cost uses measured tokens. Use this for canary comparisions, not invoices."

maria: will do. tagging follow-ups: @jake for pricing calc, @tom for telemetry aggregation, @sarah for billing/UX wording.

jake: one last thought — let's ensure the console card links to the per-route cost breakdown page (quick jump) so engs can drill into token histograms and sample prompts.

maria: yep. that drilldown should include a downloadable CSV for audits. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-notice: staging rollout of ff/cost-preview-rolling-2026 scheduled for 2026-02-12 03:00 UTC.
